crit: '34 two-class datasets with a varying level of imbalance'; 10 'were randomly chosen for the preliminary analysis', the remaining 24 used for the final analysis. 'chosen datasets vary in size, number of features and degree of imbalance, which ensures a reliable assessment of the performance. All of the datasets were taken from the KEEL [47] imbalanced data repository, and as such are publicly available.'
notes: Natural = natively two-class KEEL sets (pima, haberman); the rest are KEEL ready-made binarised files (e.g. yeast2vs4, abalone3vs11, glass0, vehicle0). Noise-injected: label noise (levels 0.0-0.20, Zhu et al. scheme) and Gaussian feature noise (levels 0.0-0.5, Sáez et al. procedure) added by the authors. modified_data_released = no: GitHub link (https://github.com/michalkoziarski/RBO) holds code, CV fold partitions and results, not stated to hold the noisy datasets themselves (they are regenerated by code); adjudicator may consider 'yes' if fold partitions count. 'random draw' refers to the random split of the 34 sets into 10 preliminary and 24 final sets, not a draw from a larger pool. Figs. 1-5 illustrate noise and oversampling on a 2D example dataset whose origin is never stated, so Synthetic/Generated not coded. Table 1 prints IR, Features, Samples only (no class counts, no minority counts); two blocks numbered 1-10 and 1-24, so row_order 11-34 = bottom block 1-24.
